title: Connection hygiene cookbook: per-language timeout, pooling, and retry patterns for streaming SDKs
creator: Ava Chen
description:
Background: Teams report inconsistent streaming reliability and surprising token-level latencies across language SDKs due to mismatched default timeouts, aggressive connection churn, and different reconnect semantics. This ticket collects concrete per-language recommendations, example configs, and a short cookbook for engineers to copy into apps.

Problem: Default transport settings differ between Python/TS/Go SDKs; users running long-lived streaming (chat/collective generation) see stalls or duplicated reconnects when servers close idle sockets or intermediate proxies reset streams. Connection pools are often either too small (throttling) or too large (exhausting ephemeral ports), and retry/backoff behavior can amplify bursts.

Goals: 1) Propose a small set of vetted defaults for timeouts, keepalive, pool sizing, and retry/backoff for each SDK. 2) Provide concrete examples (copy-paste) for Python, TypeScript, and Go covering both short request patterns and long-running streaming. 3) Document graceful-reconnect and idempotency guidance for streaming clients (how to resume or continue). 4) Ship short PRs and publish a Console runbook snippet.

Non-goals: Replace OS/network tuning docs or fully tune every cloud provider. Not changing server-side behavior in this ticket.

Acceptance criteria: 1) A single canonical doc (this ticket) with per-language recommended default values and rationale. 2) 3 example snippets (Python/TS/Go) added to our SDK example repo and linked from this ticket. 3) 1 small unit/integration test matrix demonstrating streaming reconnect resilience in CI. 4) Docs/Console snippets published and QA'd by SDK/Docs owner.
proposed_defaults:
Python defaults:
- http connect timeout: 5s
- http read/response timeout (per-chunk): 20s
- overall request deadline: 120s (where applicable)
- connection pool max size: min(100, cpu*25) for high-throughput services; default 50 for lib consumers
- keepalive (SO_KEEPALIVE) interval: 30s; keepalive probes: 3
- socket reuse: enable reuseport where available
- retry policy: 3 attempts (idempotent ops), exp backoff starting 200ms, cap 5s
- streaming reconnection: client should attempt jittered reconnect with linear backoff first 500ms, then exponential up to 8s, and switch to capped stream-fallthrough after 30s

TypeScript defaults:
- socket connect timeout: 3s
- per-chunk streaming timeout: 15s (reset on any frame)
- overall request deadline: 180s for large streaming sessions
- pool size (browser): rely on browser connection limits (use single long-lived stream)
- pool size (node): default 100 sockets, configurable via agent.maxSockets
- keepalive: enable HTTP/2 persistent connections where possible; TLS session reuse encouraged
- retry policy: 2 attempts for non-streaming; streaming reconnect heuristics similar to Python

Go defaults:
- Dial timeout: 4s
- Response header timeout: 10s
- IdleConnTimeout: 90s (preserve connections through intermediate LB idle time)
- MaxIdleConnsPerHost: 100
- KeepAlive: 30s
- Retry policy: 3 attempts with full jitter backoff (base 150ms, cap 4s)
- Streaming behavior: use context-aware reconnect with backoff and idempotency token support

Rationale: Values chosen to balance proxy/LB idle thresholds observed in common clouds, ephemeral port exhaustion trade-offs, and real user session durations for chat-like workloads.
